analysis.title: JPM TECH SKETCH: APP Revenue Breakdown Revealed!, U Getting Bought?, FWONK Getting Bought?, ABNB Q3 Growth Mode Activated, NET Q3 The Workers Party
key_insights: Tech sold off sharply the prior day, with semis (SOXX) down 12% and no sector spared. Megas were down modestly, all Internet names fell regardless of AI exposure, and Software fell with Infra and Cyber weaker than App Software.

Schilsky lists reasons tech has declined over the past month: 2027 AI capex estimates stopped rising in the Spring, monthly AI lab ARR increases peaked, hyperscaler operating cash flow is tapped out so incremental capex needs large capital raises, plus customer concentration, circularity, higher rates and crowding (long semis, short everything else).

Schilsky attributes the prior day's drop to investors being unprepared for Democratic gubernatorial wins in TX, OH and GA, remaining long crowding in semis and AI winners, performance-related forced de-grossing, retail selling (Bitcoin -5%, HOOD -10%), MSFT-neocloud headlines and Citrini.
Earnings season is over. QQQ is up 6.5% YTD and SOXX up 27% YTD. Schilsky says sentiment is poor, which he frames as bullish, but he does not know if that is enough to sustain a bottom.
APP rose 31% the prior day and is up over 50% in a week, but is still down nearly 50% YTD at a mid-teens GAAP P/E on Bull 2027 EPS. Schilsky says to seriously consider chasing it and that he would.

Schilsky estimates APP's Q3 split from call disclosures: Gaming $1.9B (+48% Y/Y) and eCommerce $276M (+140% Y/Y). He argues the Q4 guide looks easy, since the sequential eComm growth needed to hit the high end of guidance ($2.395B) is less than half of last year's Q/Q rates.

Reuters reports Unity held talks to be acquired by a consortium including Silver Lake and Saudi PIF at a valuation of about $25B, versus a market cap of about $21.5B after earnings. U trades up 5% pre-market. Schilsky asks whether this precludes a WDAY deal and whether it helps or hurts APP.

FWONK paid John Malone about 1.5% of market cap ($350M+) to cut his voting power, adopted a shareholder rights plan expiring Nov 3, 2027, and rose 10% in a weak tape. Schilsky reads this as positioning the company for a sale on its own terms.

ABNB is up 12% pre-market after Q3 room nights grew 16% Y/Y against expectations of 12-13%. Gross bookings grew 21% Y/Y, 5% above the Street, and Adj. EBITDA of $2.5B beat by 6%. A $12B buyback was authorized. Schilsky notes BKNG and EXPE are decelerating.

ABNB Q4 guide: nights at least low double-digits (Street +10%), gross bookings mid-teens (Street +13%), Adj. EBITDA margin down slightly Y/Y versus Street expecting +100 bps expansion. ABNB plans to roll out its own AI travel agent in 1H27.

NET is up 21% pre-market after Q3 revenue of $783M (+39% Y/Y), 2 points above expectations and 7 points above its own guide. cRPO grew 37%. Gross margin fell about 300 bps Y/Y. Q4 revenue guide is $845M-$846M (+37% to +38%) versus Street high end near +31-32%.
JPM's Samik raised the NET Dec-27 price target to $375 from $350 and sees GAAP profitability in 4Q FY26, ahead of the FY28 target.
JPM's Doug is Neutral on ABNB with a Dec-27 PT of $202 based on ~16x '28E FCF, looking for a better entry point.
SNAP fell 14% after ad revenue grew 4% Y/Y. It will move to MAU as its primary audience metric from Q1 2027, which Schilsky reads as a sign DAUs may decline.
Palo Alto Networks is reported by TechCrunch to be in talks to buy Clutch Security for $500M in cash plus milestones, about 50x ARR of nearly $10M.
META Muse reached 20M downloads and Instagram is showing wide-format Features in the app. Schilsky also notes T/TMUS would remove Boost from their network if SPCX buys it.

market_movers.rationale: Schilsky says to seriously consider chasing APP after Q3 disclosures. Gaming grew nearly 50% Y/Y and eComm grew triple digits, and the Q4 guide looks easy.
Doug stays Neutral with a Dec-27 PT of $202 (~16x '28E FCF) despite a strong Q3 beat, and is looking for a better entry point.
Samik raised the Dec-27 PT to $375 from $350 on accelerating growth, TAM expansion and earlier GAAP profitability.
Reuters reports takeover talks with Silver Lake and PIF at about $25B. The stock is up about 5% pre-market.
Malone's voting-power reduction plus a rights plan suggests a possible sale on the board's terms. The stock rose 10%.
Ad revenue grew 4% Y/Y, and the switch from DAU to MAU reporting is read as a negative signal.
Reported talks to buy Clutch Security for $500M cash plus milestones, about 50x ARR.

sector_views.rationale: Internet names sold off regardless of AI exposure, though Schilsky favors APP, ABNB and NET fundamentals.
SOXX fell 12% in one day amid crowded long positioning, but is still up 27% YTD.
Software fell sharply, with Infra and Cyber weaker than App Software.

earnings_insights: ABNB Q3 2026 (reported): room nights 155M, +16% Y/Y vs Street est +12-13%. Gross bookings +21% Y/Y reported and FXN, 5% above Street. Adj. EBITDA $2.5B, 6% above Street. $12B buyback authorized.

ABNB Q4 2026 guidance: nights at least low double-digits (Street est +10%), gross bookings mid-teens (Street est +13%), Adj. EBITDA margin down slightly Y/Y (Street est +100 bps expansion). JPM full-year expectation: mid-teens GBV growth, high-teens revenue growth, 36% Adj. EBITDA margin.
NET Q3 2026 (reported): revenue $783M, +39% Y/Y, about 2 points above Street and 7 points above guide. cRPO +37% Y/Y. Gross margin down about 300 bps Y/Y.
NET Q4 2026 guidance: revenue $845M-$846M (+37% to +38% Y/Y) vs Street high end near +31-32%.

APP Q3 2026 (reported): total revenue $2.185B vs $1.405B in Q3 2025. JPM estimates Gaming $1.9B (+48% Y/Y) and eCommerce $276M (+140% Y/Y), assuming management's 'nearly 50%' and 'triple-digit' growth mean those figures. Q4 2026 revenue guide high end is $2.395B.
SNAP Q3 2026 (reported): advertising revenue +4% Y/Y, stock fell 14%.
JPM Research published Q3 notes on EXPE (Q4 lower on choppy macro), LYFT (NA rides accelerate), FROG (significant beat and raise), LYV (AOI beat), SPHR (constructive venue commentary) and DKNG.
crypto_views: Bitcoin fell 5% the prior day, cited as an example of retail-related selling.

trade_ideas.rationale: Axon 3.0 is coming online, Gaming grew nearly 50% Y/Y, eComm triple-digit Y/Y, and the stock is still down nearly 50% YTD at a mid-teens GAAP P/E on Bull 2027 EPS.

risk_factors: More datacenter-related scary headlines in the short term.
AI capex estimate growth is slowing and hyperscalers must fund incremental capex through large capital raises.
Customer concentration and circularity concerns in AI.
Crowded long positioning in semis and AI winners could trigger further de-grossing.
ABNB Q4 Adj. EBITDA margin guided down slightly versus Street expectations of expansion, and EMEA developments are being monitored.
NET gross margin fell about 300 bps Y/Y and the stock remains expensive and volatile.
vol_and_positioning: Schilsky cites extreme crowding in long semis and short everything else, with performance-related forced de-grossing the prior day.
Schilsky says semis investors now know how software and internet investors felt earlier in the year.
geopolitical: Democratic wins in the TX, OH and GA governor races in the midterm elections are cited as a driver of the prior day's tech selloff.
Saudi Arabia's PIF is part of the consortium reportedly approaching Unity.

tension_points.bull_case: Sentiment is very poor, which Schilsky says should be bullish. QQQ is still up 6.5% YTD and SOXX 27% YTD, futures are higher, and the prior day's move may be a head fake.
tension_points.bear_case: AI capex estimate growth is slowing, hyperscaler operating cash flow is tapped out, and crowded long semis positioning could drive more forced de-grossing, with more scary datacenter headlines expected in the short term.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Schilsky does not state a specific level or event. He says only that more datacenter-related headlines are likely in the short term.
